title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC1LF_---1LD_1LE0RA_1RE1LB_1RD0LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC1LF_---1LD_1LE0RA_1RE1LB_1RD0LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Read as a list of digits, the tape is rewritten by markers that crawl through long blocks of 2s (proved in Lean), merge and decay, and by rare epochs that rebuild a long block at the left end; the rule for the epochs is not known yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 49,386 cells have been visited and 32,933 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: Read as runs of 1s separated by single 0s, the tape is a list of blocks of 2-runs ((110)^n) separated by marker runs: at 109 steps 1 2^10415 4 2^975 3 2^3848 6 6 2^653 3 2^244 3 2^30 6 2^116 3 2^18 6 2^66 3 2^34 6 2^42 1. The right part from 2^30 on is identical at 108 steps; only the blocks near the growing left end change.

claims.title: The marker crawls through the 2s
claims.text: Mk a b R = 0^inf D> 0 0 (110)^a 1110 (110)^b R: two sweeps take Mk a (b+1) R to Mk (a+3) b R in 24a+70 steps, for all a, b and every tape R; iterated, Mk a (b+j) R reaches Mk (a+3j) b R.

claims.title: The rewriting rules
claims.text: Read as a list of digits (runs of 1s between single 0s), every change between consecutive visits of the left end in the first 3·10<sup>8</sup> steps is one of a few local rules that keep the number of cells: 3 2 → 6 → 2 3 (the marker), 3 3 → 7 → 2 4 → 2 1 (merging and decay), 3 6 → 10 → 2 7, 3 1 → 5 → 2 2, plus fast signals (a 1 crossing a block of 2s in one sweep) and rare epochs where a long block at the left end is rebuilt (N = 2, 8, 214, 1220, 2528, 7645).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The rule that decides the epochs (block sizes 2, 8, 214, 1220, 2528, 7645) is the missing piece; see Next steps in the README.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 49,386 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A list of digits, and markers crawling through it
html: Write the tape as runs of 1s separated by single 0s, and write each run as its length. The tape becomes a list of digits, almost all 2s, with a few markers:
(2^7645 means 7645 twos in a row.) The head sweeps over the whole list and back; each round trip adds a digit at the left end.

<svg viewBox='0 0 560 130' role='img' aria-label='the marker 3 becomes 6 and then moves one digit right' style='width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:13px var(--mono)'><g fill='var(--fg)'><text x='10' y='25'>sweep 1:</text><text x='110' y='25'>2 2 2 <tspan fill='var(--head)' font-weight='700'>3</tspan> 2 2 2 2</text><text x='10' y='65'>sweep 2:</text><text x='110' y='65'>2 2 2 <tspan fill='var(--head)' font-weight='700'>6</tspan> 2 2 2</text><text x='10' y='105'>sweep 3:</text><text x='110' y='105'>2 2 2 2 <tspan fill='var(--head)' font-weight='700'>3</tspan> 2 2 2</text></g><text x='330' y='65' fill='var(--muted)'>111 0 11 = 111111 = 11 0 111</text></svg>

A marker 3 moves one digit right every two sweeps, passing through the form 6 (the same six cells with the 0 filled in). This motion is proved in Lean for blocks of any length. When a marker catches the next one they merge and decay: 3 3 → 7 → 2 4 → 2 2 1; a 1 is a fast signal that crosses a whole block of 2s in a single sweep and becomes a new marker at its end. Every rule keeps the number of cells.

Every so often a long block at the left end is rebuilt at once (an epoch); the block sizes at the epochs are 2, 8, 214, 1220, 2528, 7645. What decides them is not yet understood, so there is no map from one epoch to the next, and no estimate of whether the machine halts.

Where it could halt

Only by arriving at the blank left end of the tape in state B. In the run the head always arrives there in state D, E or F.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,386 cells (33,922 left of the start, 163 right), with a density of 1s of 0.667.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A list of digits (runs of 1s) mostly 2s, rewritten by markers 3/6 that crawl right through blocks of 2s, merge, decay into fast signals, and rare epochs that rebuild a long block; marker motion proved in Lean; open.
